Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 8, verse 1:

In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate.

Surat al-Anfal (the Spoils of War)

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿They ask you about the spoils. Say: The spoils belong to Allah and the Messenger﴾, and the rest of the verse.

The scholars differed over what is meant by *al-anfal* (the spoils of war) here, in five opinions:

The first: it refers specifically to what escapes from the disbelievers to the believers without fighting, such as a horse or a camel that runs from the disbelievers to the Muslims. According to this interpretation, *al-anfal* is what the jurists call *fay'* (property taken from the enemy without battle), which is explained in His saying: ﴿And what Allah restored to His Messenger from them, you did not spur toward it horse or camel﴾ [al-Hashr: 6]. Among those who held this view is ʿAṭāʾ ibn Abi Rabah.

The second: it refers to the *khums* (one-fifth), which is the view of Malik.

The third: it refers to one-fifth of the *khums*.

The fourth: it refers to the entire spoils (*ghanima*). This is the view of the majority, and among those who held it are Ibn ʿAbbas, Mujahid, ʿIkrimah, ʿAṭāʾ, al-Ḍaḥḥak, Qatada, ʿAṭāʾ al-Khurasani, Muqatil ibn Hayyan, and ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam, and others, as Ibn Kathir stated.

The fifth: it refers specifically to the spoils of the *sarāyā* (raiding detachments). Among those who held this view is al-Shaʿbi, and Ibn Jarir transmitted it from ʿAli ibn Salih ibn Hayy. What is meant by this view is what the leader grants to some raiding detachments as an addition to their share, beyond what the rest of the army receives. Ibn Jarir chose that *al-anfal* means the addition over the share. Ibn Kathir said: "This is supported by what was reported about the occasion of revelation of the verse, namely what Ahmad narrated, saying: Abu Muʿawiya narrated to us, Abu Ishaq al-Shaybani narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn ʿUbayd Allah al-Thaqafi, from Saʿd ibn Abi Waqqas, who said: 'When the day of Badr came, and my brother ʿUmayr was killed, I killed Saʿid ibn al-ʿAs and took his sword, which was called Dhu al-Katifa. I brought it to the Prophet (ﷺ), and he said: "Go and throw it into the spoils heap." So I returned, and I had within me what none knows except Allah, regarding the killing of my brother and the taking of my spoils. I had not gone far when the surah of al-Anfal was revealed, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Go and take your spoils."'" And Imam Ahmad also said: Aswad ibn ʿAmir narrated to us, Abu Bakr informed us, from ʿAsim ibn Abi al-Najud, from Mus'ab ibn Saʿd, from Saʿd ibn Malik, who said: "I said: O Messenger of Allah, Allah has cured me today of the polytheists, so grant me this sword. He said: 'This sword is neither yours nor mine; put it down.' So I put it down, then I returned and said: Perhaps this sword will be given to someone who does not endure my trials. Then a man called me from behind me, and I said: Has Allah revealed something about me? He said: You asked me for the sword, and it is not mine, and it has been given to me, so it is yours. And Allah revealed this verse: ﴿They ask you about the spoils. Say: The spoils belong to Allah and the Messenger﴾." Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa'i also narrated it through several chains from Abu Bakr ibn ʿAyyash, and al-Tirmidhi said: "Hasan sahih." Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi narrated similarly: Shuʿba informed us, Simak ibn Harb informed us, who said: "I heard Mus'ab ibn Saʿd narrating from Saʿd, who said: Four verses of the Qur'an were revealed concerning me. I obtained a sword on the day of Badr and came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: Grant it to me as a gift. He said: 'Put it back where you took it from,' twice. Then I returned to him, and the Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'Put it back where you took it from.' Then this verse was revealed: ﴿They ask you about the spoils﴾," and the complete hadith concerns the revelation of ﴿We have enjoined upon man kindness to his parents﴾ [al-ʿAnkabut: 8], His saying ﴿Indeed, intoxicants and gambling﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 90] and the verse of the bequest. Muslim narrated it in his Sahih from the hadith of Shuʿba. Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: ʿAbd Allah ibn Abi Bakr narrated to me, from some of the Banu Saʿida, who said: "I heard Abu Usayd Malik ibn Rabiʿa say: I obtained the sword of Ibn ʿAʾidh on the day of Badr, and that sword was called al-Mirzaban. When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) commanded the people to return what they had in their hands of the *nafl* (extra gifts), I came with it and threw it into the *nafl*. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would not refuse anything he was asked, so al-Arqam ibn Abi al-Arqam al-Makhzumi saw it, asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he gave it to him." Ibn Jarir also narrated it through another route. End of Ibn Kathir's words.

The author of this commentary, may Allah pardon him, says: The majority of scholars hold that the verse was revealed concerning the spoils of Badr, when the Companions disputed over them. Some of them said: "We are the ones who gathered the spoils and secured them, so no one else has a share in them." The elders said: "We were a reserve for you; had you been defeated, you would have sought refuge with us." So they brought their dispute before the Prophet (ﷺ). Imam Ahmad, al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah narrated from ʿUbada ibn al-Samit that it was revealed concerning that. Al-Tirmidhi said: "This is a sahih hadith." Ibn Hibban narrated it in his Sahih, and al-Hakim in his Mustadrak, and said: "Its chain is sahih according to the condition of Muslim, though they did not record it." Abu Dawud, al-Nasa'i, Ibn Hibban, al-Hakim, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Mardawayh narrated similar material through several routes from Dawud ibn Abi Hind, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbas. According to this view, which is the view of the majority, the verse is problematic with His saying: ﴿And know that whatever you gain of anything﴾ [al-Anfal: 41] and the rest of the verse.

The most evident of the opinions by which the difficulty in the verse is removed is what Abu ʿUbayd mentioned, and al-Qurtubi in his tafsir attributed it to the majority of scholars: that His saying ﴿And know that whatever you gain﴾ and the rest of the verse abrogates (*naskh*, the cancelling of an earlier ruling by a later one) His saying ﴿They ask you about the spoils﴾. However, Abu ʿUbayd's claim that the spoils of Badr were not divided into fifths, because the verse of the fifth was not revealed until after the division of the spoils of Badr, is not correct. Its invalidity is shown by what is established in Sahih Muslim from the hadith of ʿAli ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him: "I had a she-camel from my share of the spoils on the day of Badr, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had given me a she-camel from the fifth on that day," and the hadith continues. This is a sound explicit text that the spoils of Badr were divided into fifths, because ʿAli's words in this sound hadith, "on that day," are clearly referring to the day of Badr, as you see.

The conclusion is that the verse ﴿And know that whatever you gain of anything﴾ and the rest of it makes clear that the spoils are not restricted to the Messenger mentioned at the beginning of the surah, and that four-fifths of them are given to those who fought. We have already mentioned that Abu ʿUbayd said it abrogates the earlier verse, and al-Qurtubi attributed this to the majority. More clarification of this topic, God willing, will come in the discussion of His saying: ﴿And know that whatever you gain of anything﴾ and the rest of the verse.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 8, verse 2:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And when His verses are recited to them, they increase them in faith﴾ — the verse. In this noble verse there is an explicit statement that faith increases, and Allah, exalted is He, has stated this explicitly in other places,

• such as His saying: ﴿And when a surah is revealed, among them are those who say, "Which of you has this increased in faith?" As for those who believe, it has increased them in faith, and they rejoice﴾ [at-Tawbah: 124],

• and His saying: ﴿It is He who sent down tranquility into the hearts of the believers that they might increase in faith along with their faith﴾ — the verse [al-Fath: 4],

• and His saying: ﴿So that those who were given the Scripture may be certain and those who believe may increase in faith﴾ — the verse [al-Muddaththir: 31],

• and His saying: ﴿And those who are guided, He increases them in guidance﴾ — the verse [Muhammad: 17].

These verses indicate by implication (dalalat al-iltizam) that faith also decreases, because whatever increases can decrease. This is stated explicitly in the authentic hadiths of intercession, such as His saying (ﷺ): "There will come out of the Fire whoever said, 'There is no god but Allah,' and in his heart is an atom's weight of faith," and the like.

The author said in (Daf' Iham al-Idtirab 'an Ayat al-Kitab):

(p-291) In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Surah al-Anfal

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿The believers are only those who, when Allah is mentioned, their hearts tremble﴾ — the verse.

This verse indicates that the trembling of hearts at the hearing of the mention of Allah is among the signs of the believers.

But another verse has come that indicates the opposite, namely His saying: ﴿Those who believe, and whose hearts are assured by the remembrance of Allah. Unquestionably, by the remembrance of Allah hearts are assured﴾ [ar-Ra'd: 28].

Thus the contradiction between tranquility (ṭuma'nīnah) and the trembling of hearts is apparent.

The answer to this is that tranquility occurs through the expansion of the breast by knowledge of monotheism (tawhid), while trembling occurs at the fear of deviation and of going astray from guidance, as His saying, may He be exalted, indicates: ﴿From it the skins of those who fear their Lord shiver; then their skins and their hearts soften to the remembrance of Allah﴾ [az-Zumar: 23], and His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Our Lord, do not let our hearts deviate after You have guided us﴾ — the verse [ar-Ra'd: 8].

And His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And those who give what they give while their hearts are fearful that they will return to their Lord﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 60].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 8, verse 11:

قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿إذْ يُغَشِّيكُمُ النُّعاسَ أمَنَةً مِنهُ﴾ .

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿When He covered you with drowsiness as a security from Him﴾.

He, may He be exalted, mentions in this noble verse that He cast drowsiness upon the believers so that He would make their hearts secure, not fearful of their enemy; for the one who is frightened and alarmed is not overcome by drowsiness. The apparent context of this verse indicates that this drowsiness was cast upon them on the day of Badr, because the discussion here concerns the battle of Badr, as is well known.

And He mentioned in Surat Al 'Imran that drowsiness also overcame them on the day of Uhud, in His saying, may He be exalted, regarding the battle of Uhud: ﴿Then He sent down upon you, after distress, security in the form of drowsiness﴾ [3:154] to the end of the verse.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 8, verse 19:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿If you seek a decision, then the decision has certainly come to you.﴾

The meaning of "al-fath" (decision/judgment) here in this verse, according to the majority of scholars (jumhur al-'ulama'), is "al-hukm" (judgment). This is because when the Quraysh intended to set out for the battle of Badr, they clung to the curtains of the Ka'bah and claimed that they were the custodians of the Sacred House of Allah, that they gave water to the pilgrims, and similar things, and that Muhammad ﷺ had divided the community, severed the ties of kinship, made foolish the forefathers, and disparaged the religion. Then they asked Allah to judge between them and the Prophet ﷺ, by destroying the wrongdoer among them and granting victory to the one in the right. So Allah judged accordingly: He destroyed them, granted him victory, and revealed the verse.

What indicates that the meaning of "al-fath" here is "al-hukm" is that He, may He be exalted, followed it with something that shows the address is to the disbelievers of Makkah, namely His saying: ﴿And if you cease, it is better for you; and if you return, We will return.﴾ [al-Anfal: 19]. This is clarified by the use of "al-fath" in the sense of "al-hukm" in the Qur'an in His saying about Shu'ayb and his people: ﴿Upon Allah we have relied. Our Lord, decide between us and our people in truth, and You are the best of deciders.﴾ [al-A'raf: 89]. That is, judge between us and our people in truth, and You are the best of judges. This is supported by His saying, may He be exalted, about Shu'ayb in the same story: ﴿And if there is a group among you who have believed in that with which I have been sent and a group who have not believed, then be patient until Allah judges between us, and He is the best of judges.﴾ [al-A'raf: 87].

This is the dialect of Himyar, for they call the judge "fattah" (one who decides) and the judgeship "fattahah."

From it is the saying of the poet (al-Wafir meter):

Ala ablighu Bani 'Amrin rasulan bi-anni 'an futahatikum ghaniyyun

That is: I am independent of your judgeship and your decision. As for what some scholars have mentioned, that the address in His saying ﴿If you seek a decision﴾ is to the believers, meaning you seek victory and support from Allah, and that the address in His following saying ﴿And if you cease, it is better for you﴾ is to the disbelievers, this is not apparent, as you see.

The author said in (Daf' Iham al-Idtirab 'an Ayat al-Kitab):

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O you who have believed, respond to Allah and to the Messenger when he calls you to that which gives you life﴾ — the verse.

This verse, by its apparent meaning, indicates that obedience to the Messenger, which is the response to him, is obligatory only when he calls us to that which gives us life. A parallel to it is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And they will not disobey you in what is right﴾ [al-Mumtahanah: 12].

Yet other verses have come that indicate the obligation of following him absolutely, without any condition, such as His saying: ﴿And whatever the Messenger gives you, take it; and whatever he forbids you, refrain from﴾ [al-Hashr: 7], and His saying: ﴿Say, "If you should love Allah, then follow me; Allah will love you"﴾ (p-292) — the verse [Ali 'Imran: 31], and His saying: ﴿Whoever obeys the Messenger has obeyed Allah﴾ [an-Nisa': 80].

The apparent way of reconciling these, and Allah knows best, is that the verses of absoluteness make clear that he, peace and blessings be upon him, calls us only to that which gives us life, of the good of this world and the Hereafter. Thus the condition mentioned in His saying ﴿when he calls you﴾ is fulfilled in the call of the Prophet (ﷺ) because of his infallibility, as indicated by His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Nor does he speak from desire. It is not but a revelation revealed﴾ [an-Najm: 3–4].

The conclusion is that the verse ﴿when he calls you to that which gives you life﴾ makes clear that there is no obedience except to one who calls to what pleases Allah, and that the other verses have explained that the Prophet (ﷺ) never calls except to that, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him.

The Words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And know that your wealth and your children are only a trial, and that with Allah is a great reward﴾.

In this noble verse, Allah, the Exalted, commands people to know that their wealth and their children are a trial (fitnah) by which they are tested: will wealth and children become a cause of falling into what does not please Allah? In another place He added that spouses too are a trial, just like wealth and children. He therefore commanded a person to be wary of them lest they lead him into what does not please Allah. Then He commanded him, if he becomes aware of something from those enemies who are the closest of people to him and the most special to him, namely children and spouses, that displeases him, to pardon them, overlook their faults, and not hold them to account. Thus he should be wary of them at first, and overlook (p-52) what occurs from them of some matter. This is in His words in "at-Taghabun": ﴿O you who believe, indeed among your spouses and your children are enemies to you, so beware of them. But if you pardon and overlook and forgive, then indeed Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ ﴿Your wealth and your children are only a trial, and Allah has with Him a great reward﴾ [at-Taghabun: 14, 15].

He also explicitly forbade the believers, in another place, from being diverted by wealth and children from the remembrance of Him, Glorified and Exalted, and that whoever falls into that is the loser, defrauded in his own shares. This is His words, Exalted is He: ﴿O you who believe, let not your wealth or your children divert you from the remembrance of Allah. And whoever does that, then those are the losers﴾ [al-Munafiqun: 9]. The meaning of fitnah in the verses is testing and trial, which is one of the meanings of fitnah in the Qur'an.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 8, verse 31:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿They say: "We have heard. If we wished, we could say the like of this."﴾ and so on.

We have already explained, before these verses, the passages that clearly declare their lie and the inability of Allah to let them produce the like of it, so there is no need to repeat them here. As for His saying here, concerning them, in this verse: ﴿This is nothing but the fables of the former peoples﴾ [al-Anfal: 31], Allah has refuted their lie and their fabrication in this regard in many verses, such as His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And they say, "Fables of the former peoples, which he has had written down, and they are dictated to him morning and evening."﴾ ﴿Say: "It was sent down by the One who knows the secret in the heavens and the earth. Indeed, He is ever Forgiving and Merciful."﴾ [al-Furqan: 5, 6]. The One who knows the secret in the heavens and the earth is far too exalted to have sent down what would be the fables of the former peoples. And like His saying: ﴿And We know that they say, "It is only a human who teaches him." The tongue of the one they refer to is foreign, while this is a clear Arabic tongue.﴾ [al-Nahl: 103], along with other verses.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And when they said, "O Allah, if this is indeed the truth from You, then rain down upon us stones from the sky, or bring us a painful punishment."﴾

In this noble verse, He mentions what shows that the disbelievers of Makkah were in the utmost ignorance, since they said, ﴿rain down upon us﴾, and so on [al-Anfal: 32], and did not say, "Guide us to it." Other verses also indicate this, such as:

• His saying about them: ﴿And they said, "Our Lord, hasten to us our portion [of punishment] before the Day of Reckoning."﴾ [Sad: 16],

• His saying: ﴿And they ask you to hasten the punishment﴾, and so on [al-Hajj: 47],

• His saying: ﴿And if We delay the punishment from them for a counted period, they will surely say, "What is holding it back?"﴾ [Hud: 8]. He also mentioned something similar about some of the earlier nations,

• such as His saying about the people of Shu'ayb: ﴿So cause a piece of the sky to fall upon us, if you are among the truthful.﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 187],

• and His saying about the people of Salih: ﴿O Salih, bring us what you threaten us with, if you are among the messengers.﴾ [al-A'raf: 77]. More clarification of this, Allah willing, will come in the surah "Sa'ala sa'il" [al-Ma'arij: 1].

The author said, in *Daf' Iham al-Idtirab 'an Ayat al-Kitab* (Removing the Appearance of Contradiction from the Verses of the Book):

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And Allah would not punish them while you are among them, and Allah would not punish them while they seek forgiveness﴾. This noble verse indicates that the disbelievers of Makkah had two safeguards, by which Allah would keep the punishment away from them:

The first: his ﷺ presence among them, because Allah does not destroy a nation while its Prophet is among them.

The second: their seeking forgiveness from Allah. His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And what is wrong with them that Allah should not punish them, while they bar access to al-Masjid al-Haram﴾ [8:34] indicates the opposite of this.

The answer has four aspects:

The first, which is the choice of Ibn Jarir, who reported it from Qatadah, al-Suddi and Ibn Zayd, is that both safeguards have ceased to exist. The Prophet ﷺ left from among them as a emigrant, and their seeking forgiveness is non-existent because they persisted in disbelief.

So the circumstantial clause (*hal*, a clause describing the state of the subject at the time of the action) is intended to mean that the punishment would not descend upon them in a state of seeking forgiveness, were they to seek it, nor in a state of their Prophet being present among them. But he left from among them, and they did not seek forgiveness because of their disbelief.

It is known that the *hal* is a restriction on its governing verb and a description of its subject. So seeking forgiveness, for example, is a restriction on the negation of punishment. However, they did not bring the restriction. Thus the meaning is established as: "And Allah would not punish them while they seek forgiveness, if they sought it." After both conditions ceased, He punished them by killing and capture on the Day of Badr, as His saying, exalted is He, indicates: ﴿And We will surely make them taste the lesser punishment before the greater punishment﴾ [32:21].

The second aspect: the intended meaning of His saying ﴿while they seek forgiveness﴾ is the seeking of forgiveness by the believers who were oppressed in Makkah. In this case the meaning is that after his ﷺ departure, the believers' seeking of forgiveness was a cause for lifting the worldly punishment from the disbelievers, who were hastening for punishment by their saying: ﴿So rain down upon us stones from the sky﴾ [8:32], and so on.

According to this view, the seeking of forgiveness is attributed to the whole collective of the people of Makkah, while the specific reference is to the believers among them. A parallel to this verse in this sense is His saying: ﴿So they hamstrung the she-camel﴾ [7:77], although the one who hamstrung it was one of them, as His saying indicates: ﴿So they called their companion, and he took it and hamstrung it﴾ [54:29].

- And His saying: ﴿Have you not considered how Allah created seven heavens in layers? And made the moon therein a light﴾ [71:15–16]. That is, He made the moon within the collective of them, in the specific sense of the heaven in which the moon is, since He did not place a moon in each heaven.

- And His saying: ﴿O assembly of jinn and mankind, did there not come to you messengers from among you?﴾ [6:130]. That is, from among your collective, specifically mankind according to the more correct view, since there are no messengers from among the jinn.

As for the many scholars' illustration of the use of the collective term while only part of it is intended, by His saying: ﴿From both of them emerge the pearl and the coral﴾ [55:22], claiming that the meaning of His saying "from them both" is from their collective, specifically the salt sea, since no pearl or coral emerges from the fresh water, this is a false view, contradicted by the explicit text of the Mighty Qur'an.

Allah has explicitly stated the extraction of pearl and coral from both seas, when He said: ﴿And the two seas are not alike: this one is fresh, sweet and pleasant to drink, and this one is salty and bitter. And from each you eat tender meat and extract ornaments which you wear﴾ [35:12].

His saying ﴿and from each﴾ is a clear text that both the fresh and the salty are intended together, and His saying ﴿ornaments which you wear﴾ refers to the pearl and the coral.

According to this view, the worldly punishment is averted from them by Allah through the seeking of forgiveness by the believers who were living among them. And His saying: ﴿And what is wrong with them that Allah should not punish them﴾ [8:34] means: after the departure of the believers, whose seeking of forgiveness was the cause for averting the worldly punishment. So after their departure, Allah punished the people of Makkah in this world by empowering His Messenger ﷺ over them, until he conquered Makkah. What confirms that Allah averts the worldly punishment from the disbelievers because of the presence of Muslims among them is what happened at the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah, as He explained by His saying: ﴿And if not for believing men and believing women whom you did not know, that you might trample them and thereby there would come upon you blame without knowledge [from them]—that Allah might admit into His mercy whom He wills. If they had been separated, We would have surely punished those who disbelieved among them with painful punishment﴾ [48:25].

His saying ﴿If they had been separated﴾ means: if the disbelievers had been separated from the Muslims, We would have punished the disbelievers by giving the Muslims power over them. But We withheld this worldly punishment from the disbelievers because the believers were not distinguishable from them, as He explained by His saying: ﴿And if not for believing men and believing women﴾, and so on.

Ibn Jarir reported this view from Ibn 'Abbas, al-Dahhak, Abu Malik and Ibn Abza. The essence of this view is that when the disbelievers of Makkah said: ﴿O Allah, if this is the truth from You, then rain down upon us stones from the sky﴾ [8:32], Allah sent down His saying: ﴿And Allah would not punish them while you are among them﴾. Then, when the Prophet ﷺ emigrated, a group of Muslims remained in Makkah seeking forgiveness from Allah and worshipping Him, so Allah sent down: ﴿And Allah would not punish them while they seek forgiveness﴾. Then when the remaining Muslims left Makkah, Allah, exalted is He, sent down: ﴿And what is wrong with them that Allah should not punish them﴾ [8:34], meaning: what reason remains for them that would ward off Allah's punishment from them, when the Prophet ﷺ and the believers have left from among them? Accordingly, the verse is like His saying: ﴿Fight them; Allah will punish them by your hands﴾ [9:14].

The third aspect: the intended meaning of His saying ﴿while they seek forgiveness﴾ is the disbelievers of Makkah. According to this, the overall meaning is that Allah, exalted is He, averts the worldly punishment from them because of their seeking forgiveness. As for the punishment of the Hereafter, it will certainly befall them. So His saying ﴿And Allah would not punish them﴾ means in this world, in the state of their seeking forgiveness. And His saying ﴿And what is wrong with them that Allah should not punish them﴾ means in the Hereafter, and they were disbelievers in this world. Ibn Jarir reported this view from Ibn 'Abbas.

According to this view, the deeds of the disbeliever benefit him in this world, as a group of scholars interpreted His saying: ﴿And He found Allah with him, and He paid him in full his account﴾ [24:39], meaning: He rewarded him for his good deeds in this world. This is the explicit meaning of His saying: ﴿Whoever desires the worldly life and its adornment, We will pay them in full for their deeds therein﴾ [11:15], and His saying: ﴿Those are the ones whose deeds have become void in this world and the Hereafter﴾ [2:217], and His saying: ﴿And We will confront what they did of deeds and make them scattered dust﴾ [25:23], and similar verses, which indicate the nullity of the disbeliever's deeds from their very root. As Allah explained by His saying: ﴿Their deeds have become void in this world and the Hereafter﴾ [2:217], making both abodes a container for the nullity and annihilation of their deeds. The verification of this matter will come, if Allah wills, in Surat Hud.

The fourth aspect: the meaning of His saying ﴿while they seek forgiveness﴾ is "while they submit (become Muslims)". That is: Allah would not punish them, and it had already been foreknown by Him that among them are those who will submit and seek Allah's forgiveness for their disbelief. According to this view, His saying ﴿And what is wrong with them that Allah should not punish them﴾ refers to those for whom wretchedness had preceded, such as Abu Jahl and his companions, who were punished by being killed on the Day of Badr.

Ibn Jarir reported the meaning of this view from 'Ikrimah and Mujahid. As for what Ibn Jarir reported from 'Ikrimah and al-Hasan al-Basri, that His saying ﴿And what is wrong with them that Allah should not punish them﴾ abrogates His saying ﴿And Allah would not punish them while they seek forgiveness﴾, its falsity is evident, because His saying, exalted is He, ﴿And Allah would not punish them﴾, and so on, is a report from Allah that He does not punish them while they are seeking forgiveness. A report cannot be abrogated in the law, by the consensus (*ijma'*) of Muslims. The most apparent of these views are the first two.

Among them is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿If there are among you twenty patient ones, they will overcome two hundred﴾ [8:65], and so on.

The apparent meaning of this verse is that each Muslim is obligated to endure against ten disbelievers. Allah, exalted is He, has mentioned what indicates the opposite of this by His saying: ﴿Now Allah has lightened your burden, and He knows that among you there is weakness. So if there are among you one hundred patient ones, they will overcome two hundred﴾ [8:66], and so on.

The answer to this is that the first is abrogated by the second, as indicated by His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Now Allah has lightened your burden﴾, and so on [8:66]. And Allah, exalted is He, knows best.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 8, verse 34:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And what is [the matter] with them that Allah should not punish them while they bar [people] from the Sacred Mosque, and they were not its guardians? Its guardians are only the God-fearing (al-muttaqun), but most of them do not know.﴾

In this noble verse, Allah, exalted is He, explicitly negates the guardianship (wilayah) of the disbelievers over the Sacred Mosque, and affirms it exclusively for the God-fearing (al-muttaqin). He clarified this meaning in His saying: ﴿It is not for the polytheists to maintain the mosques of Allah while they testify against themselves to disbelief. Those—their deeds have become worthless, and in the Fire they will abide eternally.﴾ ﴿Only one who believes in Allah and the Last Day, establishes prayer, gives zakah, and fears none but Allah—those are expected to be among the guided.﴾ [al-Tawbah: 17, 18].

The commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 8, verse 35:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Their prayer at the House was nothing but whistling and clapping of hands﴾.

Al-mukaa' (المُكاء) is whistling (al-safir), and al-tasdiyah (التَّصْدِيَةُ) is clapping (al-tasfiq). Some scholars said: what is intended by their whistling and clapping is confusion (al-takhlit), so that people would not hear the Qur'an from the Prophet (ﷺ). This is supported by His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And those who disbelieve say: Do not listen to this Qur'an, and make noise during it, that you may prevail﴾ [Fussilat: 26].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 8, verse 41 (part 1 of 7):

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And know that whatever you acquire as spoils of war, a fifth of it belongs to Allah, and to the Messenger, and to the near relatives, the orphans, the needy, and the wayfarer﴾.

The apparent meaning of this noble verse is that everything the Muslims seize from the wealth of the disbelievers is subject to the one-fifth division (takhmis) as specified in the verse, whether or not they pursued it with horses and riding camels. However, in Surat al-Hashr He, exalted is He, made clear that what Allah granted to His Messenger from what the Muslims did not pursue with horses and riding camels is not divided into fifths, and its disbursement channels, which He explained, are as the channels of the fifth of the spoils mentioned here. This is in His saying, concerning the property of Banu al-Nadir: ﴿And whatever Allah restored to His Messenger from them, you did not spur horse or camel for it﴾ to the end of the verse [6]. Then He explained that the ruling applies to everything Allah restored to His Messenger from all the towns, by His saying: ﴿Whatever Allah restored to His Messenger from the people of the towns belongs to Allah and to the Messenger﴾ to the end of the verse [7].

Know first that most scholars distinguished between fay' and ghanima. They said: fay' is what Allah facilitated for the Muslims from the wealth of the disbelievers without taking it from them by force, like the fay' of Banu al-Nadir, who submitted to the judgment of the Prophet ﷺ and yielded to him their persons and wealth to do with as he wished, due to the intense terror that Allah had cast into their hearts. He ﷺ permitted them to depart with what they could carry on camels, other than weapons. As for ghanima, it is what the Muslims seized from the disbelievers by dominance and force. This distinction is understood from His saying: ﴿And know that whatever you acquire as spoils of war﴾ to the end of the verse, together with His saying: ﴿So you did not spur horse or camel for it﴾. Indeed His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So you did not spur horse or camel for it﴾ to the end of the verse, is evident that it intends to show the difference between what they pursued with horses and camels and what they did not pursue, as you see.

The distinction mentioned between ghanima and fay' was set down by Shaykh Ahmad al-Badawi al-Shinqiti in his versified work on the military expeditions, with his words concerning the expedition of Banu al-Nadir, in the meter of rajaz:

"Their fay', and fay' is in al-Anfal, what was not taken by fighting.
As for ghanima, it is by stripping (ziḥāf), and seizing by force is at the ziḥāf."

For the best of those sent [i.e., the Prophet ﷺ] etc.

His saying "wa-fay'uhum" is the subject (mubtada'), its predicate being "li-khayri mursal"; and his saying "wa'l-fay' fi'l-anfal... etc." is a parenthetical statement between the subject and predicate, by which he explained the difference between ghanima and fay'. On this view there is no difficulty in the verses, because the verse "And know that whatever you acquire as spoils of war" mentions the ruling on ghanima, and the verse "what Allah restored to His Messenger" mentions the ruling on fay', and the reason for the difference between the two matters is indicated by His saying: "So you did not spur horse or camel for it," i.e., how could it be ghanima for you, when you did not labor for it and did not seize it by force from its owners?

Some scholars said: ghanima and fay' are one and the same; everything taken from the disbelievers in any manner is both ghanima and fay'. This is the view of Qatada, may Allah have mercy on him, and it is the well-known usage in the language, for the Arabs apply the term fay' to ghanima. From this is the saying of Muhalhil ibn Rabi'a al-Taghlibi:

"No, by my father Jalila, we did not fay' (acquire) from the herd of camels that were hobbled,
But we beat the people severely upon their backs and throats."

He means that they did not busy themselves with driving off the spoils, but with killing the men. So his word "afa'na" means "ghanimna" (we acquired as spoil). This meaning is supported by His saying: ﴿And what your right hand possesses of what Allah has restored to you﴾ [al-Ahzab: 50]; for the apparent meaning of this noble verse includes all captives, even if they were taken by force. However, the well-known terminology among scholars is the distinction we have already mentioned between them, and the earlier verse of al-Hashr supports it. According to Qatada's view, the verse of al-Hashr is problematic alongside this verse of al-Anfal, and because of that problem Qatada, may Allah the Exalted have mercy on him, said that the verse "And know that whatever you acquire as spoils of war" abrogates the verse "And what Allah restored to His Messenger." This view which he held, may Allah have mercy on him, is undoubtedly false, and nothing compelled Qatada, may Allah have mercy on him, to this view except his claim that fay' and ghanima are identical. Had he distinguished between them as others did, it would have been known that the verse of al-Anfal concerns ghanima and the verse of al-Hashr concerns fay', and there would be no difficulty. The reason the said view is invalid: the verse "And know that whatever you acquire as spoils of war" was revealed after the Battle of Badr, before the division of the spoils of Badr, as evidenced by the authentic hadith of Ali in Sahih Muslim, which indicates that the spoils of Badr were divided into fifths; and the verse of the fifth which Allah legislated is this one. As for the verse of al-Hashr, it was revealed concerning the expedition of Banu al-Nadir by the consensus of scholars, and the expedition of Banu al-Nadir came after the Battle of Badr by the consensus of the Muslims (p-56), and there is no dispute about this whatsoever. From this it becomes clear that Qatada's view, may Allah the Exalted have mercy on him, is not correct. And it has become clear to you that on the view of distinguishing between ghanima and fay' there is no difficulty in the verses; and likewise on the view of those who hold that the matter of spoils and fay' is referred to the judgment of the imam, there is no contradiction, according to his view, between the verse of al-Hashr and the verse of the fifth, when the imam sees fit. And Allah knows best.

* *

Issues arising from the rulings of this noble verse

The first issue: Know that the majority of Muslim scholars hold that four-fifths of the spoils belong to the warriors who acquired them, and the imam does not have the right to assign that spoil to others. This is indicated by His saying: "whatever you acquire" — it indicates that it is spoil belonging to them. When He said: "a fifth of it belongs to Allah," we know that the remaining four-fifths belong to them and not to others. A parallel to this is His saying: "If he has no child and his parents inherit from him, then his mother has a third," i.e., and to his father the remaining two-thirds, by consensus. Likewise His saying: "a fifth of it belongs to Allah," i.e., and to the spoilers is what remains. This view is the truth beyond doubt. Several scholars have related consensus on it, and among those who related the consensus of the Muslims on it are Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn 'Abd al-Barr, al-Dawudi, al-Mazari, al-Qadi 'Iyad, and Ibn al-'Arabi. The reports with this meaning are numerous. Some people of knowledge disagreed, and this is the view of many Malikis, and al-Mazari, may Allah have mercy on him, also reported it from them. They said: the imam may spend the spoils on whatever he wishes of the interests of the Muslims, and withhold them from the warrior spoilers.

They argued for this with evidences, among them His saying: ﴿They ask you about the spoils. Say: the spoils belong to Allah and the Messenger﴾ to the end of the verse [al-Anfal: 1]. They said: al-anfal means all the spoils, and the verse is decisive (muhkama), not abrogated. They also argued by what occurred at the conquest of Mecca and the story of Hunayn. They said: he ﷺ conquered Mecca by force with ten thousand fighters, and conferred favor upon its people and returned it to them, and did not make it spoil or divide it among the army. Had the division of the four-fifths among the army been obligatory, he ﷺ would have done so when he conquered Mecca. They said: likewise the spoils of Hawazin at the Battle of Hunayn: he gave from them very great gifts, and did not give the Ansar from them, although they were among the best of the fighters who went out with him ﷺ. Shaykh Ahmad al-Badawi al-Shinqiti alluded to his gifts from the spoils of Hawazin at the Battle of Hunayn in his versified work on the expeditions, in the expedition of Hunayn, with his words in rajaz:

(p-57)
"He gave gifts that testified to generosity on that day, to him, and were not withheld.
He gave gifts that shamed the rain-clouds, when they filled the wide plain with cattle,
About two thousand she-camels from them, and what filled between two mountains of sheep,
For a man and a Bedouin, what for his fellow and his silver and his property..."
etc.

They said: If it were obligatory to divide the four-fifths among the army that acquired them, he ﷺ would not have given two thousand she-camels from the spoils of Hawazin to non-warriors, nor would he have given what filled the space between two mountains of sheep to Safwan ibn Umayya. On that day he also gave al-Aqra' ibn Habis al-Tamimi one hundred camels, and likewise 'Uyayna ibn Hisn al-Fazari, until al-'Abbas ibn Mirdas al-Sulami became jealous of that and composed his famous poem:

"Do you place my plunder and the plunder of the slaves
between 'Uyayna and al-Aqra'?
Hisn and Habis would not surpass Mirdas in an assembly,
and I was not below either of them, and whoever is lowered today is not raised.
Indeed I was in war a man of resolve, yet I was not given anything, nor was I withheld,
except camels I was given, counted as their four legs,
and they were plunder; I made up for them by my charge on the mare in the open plain,
and by waking the people when they sleep, when men are at rest, I do not rest."

They said: If the division of the four-fifths among the warriors who acquired them were obligatory, then 'Uyayna and al-Aqra' would not have been preferred in the gift from the spoils over al-'Abbas ibn Mirdas at the beginning, before he composed his poem mentioned above.

The response from the majority to these arguments is as follows. The answer regarding the verse "They ask you about the spoils" is what we have already presented: it has been abrogated by His saying: "And know that whatever you acquire as spoils of war" [al-Anfal: 41]. Al-Qurtubi attributed this to the majority of scholars. As for what occurred at the conquest of Mecca, the answer comes from several aspects:

The first: some scholars claimed that Mecca was not conquered by force, but its people took safety (aman) from him ﷺ. Among those who said this is al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him.

Those who held this view argued by his ﷺ saying: "Whoever enters the house of Abu Sufyan is safe," which is established in the Sahih. This disagreement concerns whether the Prophet ﷺ took Mecca by force — which is the view of the majority — or took safety for it; and safety is similar to a truce (sulh). Shaykh Ahmad al-Badawi al-Shinqiti set this down in his work on the expeditions with his words, concerning the Conquest, meaning Mecca, in rajaz:

"They differed regarding it: it was said it was taken in safety, and it was said it was taken by force and compulsion.
The truth is that it was conquered by force, as its verification will come, God willing."

Among the most evident answers regarding what occurred at the conquest of Mecca is that Mecca is not like other lands, because it is sacred by the sanctity of Allah from the day He created the heavens and the earth until the Day of Resurrection; it was made lawful for him ﷺ only for an hour of a day, and was not made lawful for anyone before him or after him. Whatever is of this standing is not like other lands which do not have this great sanctity.

As for what occurred in the story of Hunayn, the answer to it is clear: the Prophet ﷺ sought the willing consent of the warriors regarding the spoils, in order to win over with them the hearts of those whose hearts were to be reconciled, for the public interest of Islam and the Muslims. This is indicated by the fact that when he ﷺ heard that some of the Ansar said: "He withholds from us and gives to Quraysh, while our swords are dripping with their blood," he gathered them and spoke to them his famous speech, extremely eloquent in its beauty. Among what he said to them was: "Are you not content, O assembly of the Ansar, that the people should go away with sheep and camels, while you return with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to your dwellings?" — to the end of his speech. The people were pleased, their hearts were content, and they said: "We are content with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ as our portion and share." This is established in the Sahih. Shaykh Ahmad al-Badawi al-Shinqiti praised the excellence of this speech that he addressed to them ﷺ in his work on the expeditions, with his words in the expedition of Hunayn, in rajaz:

"He entrusted the Ansar, the best of all creatures, to their religion, when he reconciled those to be reconciled.
They were displeased with him for withholding from them, so the Prophet sent for whoever gathered them,
And he said a word like the unique necklace, whose string of speech grew weak from its arrangement."

The conclusion: four-fifths of the spoils over which the army urged on horses and riding camels belong, in verification beyond doubt, to the warrior spoilers. This is the view of the majority. You have learned the answer to the arguments of those who oppose this. Some scholars say: it is not permissible for the imam to grant anyone any part of these four-fifths, because they are the property of the spoilers. This is the view of Malik.

(p-59) Some scholars held that the imam may give some of it as a special portion (nafl) from his own judgment (ijtihad), and this is the stronger view in terms of evidence. Further clarification of this will come, God willing.

* *

The second issue: clarifying the matter of the uses (masarif) of the one-fifth (khums) taken from the spoils before division. The apparent meaning of the noble verse is that it is divided into six shares: a share for God, exalted and high; a share for the Messenger ﷺ; a share for the near kin (dhu al-qurba); a share for the orphans; a share for the needy (masakin); and a share for the wayfarer (ibn al-sabil).

Some people of knowledge said this. Abu Ja'far al-Razi narrated from al-Rabi', from Abu al-Aliyah al-Riyahi, who said: "The Messenger of God ﷺ would be brought the spoils, and he would divide them into five; four-fifths of them would go to those who were present at the battle. Then the one-fifth would be taken, and he would put his hand into it and take what his palm grasped, and he would set it aside for the Ka'bah, which is the share of God. Then he would divide what remained into five shares: one share for the Messenger ﷺ, one share for the near kin, one share for the orphans, one share for the needy, and one share for the wayfarer."

According to this view, the share of God, exalted and high, is set aside for the Ka'bah. The weakness of this view is not hidden, because there is no evidence for it.

Some of those who held this view said that the share of God, exalted and high, is returned to those in need.

The verified position is that the share of God, exalted and high, and the share of the Messenger ﷺ are one. Mentioning His name, exalted and high, is an opening of speech for glorification. Among those who held this view was Ibn 'Abbas, as al-Dahhak transmitted it from him. This is also the view of Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyyah, al-Hasan al-Basri, al-Sha'bi, 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah, 'Abd Allah ibn Buraydah, Qatadah, Mughirah, and others, as Ibn Kathir transmitted it from them.

The evidence for the soundness of this view is what al-Bayhaqi narrated with a sound chain, from 'Abd Allah ibn Shaqiq, from a man, who said: "I came to the Prophet ﷺ while he was at Wadi al-Qura, and he was showing a horse. I said: 'O Messenger of God, what do you say about the spoils?' He said: 'For God is its one-fifth, and four-fifths of it are for the army.' I said: 'Is anyone more entitled to it than anyone else?' He said: 'No, not even the arrow you take out of your quiver; you are not more entitled to it than your Muslim brother.'" This is a clear proof of what we have mentioned.

It is also supported by what Imam Ahmad narrated from al-Miqdam ibn Ma'dikarib al-Kindi, that he sat with 'Ubadah ibn al-Samit, Abu al-Darda', and al-Harith ibn Mu'awiyah al-Kindi, may God be pleased with them, and they discussed the hadith of the Messenger of God ﷺ. Abu al-Darda' said to 'Ubadah: "O 'Ubadah, the words of the Messenger of God ﷺ in such-and-such a battle concerning the fifths..." 'Ubadah said: "The Messenger of God ﷺ led them in prayer in a battle, facing a camel from the booty. When he finished the salam, the Messenger of God ﷺ stood up, took a tuft of its hair between his fingers, and said: 'This is from your spoils, and I have no share in it except my share with you, and the one-fifth, and the one-fifth is returned to you. So return the thread and the needle, and what is larger than that and smaller. Do not misappropriate (ghull), for misappropriation is a shame and a fire upon its people in this world and the next. Strive against the people for the sake of God, near and far, and do not fear the blame of any blamer for God's sake. Establish the limits of God in travel and at home. Strive for God, for jihad is one of the gates of Paradise, a great gate by which God rescues from distress and grief.'"

Ibn Kathir said, after citing this hadith of Ahmad from 'Ubadah ibn al-Samit: "This is a great hasan hadith, and I have not seen it in any of the Six Books through this chain. But Imam Ahmad, Abu Dawud, and al-Nasa'i also narrated, from the hadith of 'Amr ibn Shu'ayb, from his father, from his grandfather 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr, from the Messenger of God ﷺ, something similar in the account of the one-fifth and the prohibition of misappropriation."

And from 'Amr ibn 'Abasah: "That the Messenger of God ﷺ led them in prayer facing a camel from the booty, and when he finished the salam, he took a tuft of hair from this camel and said: 'It is not lawful for me from your spoils, even the like of this, except the one-fifth, and the one-fifth is returned to you.'" Narrated by Abu Dawud and al-Nasa'i.

Once you know that the verified position is that the one-fifth during the lifetime of the Prophet ﷺ is divided into five shares, because the name of God is mentioned for glorification and to open speech with it, while everything belongs to Him, exalted and high, know that the Prophet ﷺ would spend his share, which is one-fifth of the one-fifth, on the interests of the Muslims. The proof is his saying in the hadiths we have cited above: "and the one-fifth is returned to you," and this is the truth.

This is supported by what is established in the Sahih: that he used to take the provision of his year from the fay' of Banu al-Nadir, as will come, God willing.

As for after his death, and his departure to the Highest Companion, may the blessings and peace of God be upon him, some scholars say that his share lapses upon his death.

Among those who said this is Abu Hanifah, may God have mercy on him, and Ibn Jarir chose this view.

Abu Hanifah also held that the share of the near kin lapses upon his ﷺ death.

The sound view is that his ﷺ share remains, and that the imam of the Muslims spends it on what the Messenger of God ﷺ used to spend it on, namely the interests of the Muslims.

Some scholars said that his ﷺ share goes to whoever holds authority after him. This was narrated from Abu Bakr, 'Ali, Qatadah, and a group. Ibn Kathir said: "A marfu' hadith has also come concerning it."

The author of this commentary, may God pardon him, says: The apparent meaning is that this view, in substance, returns to what we have mentioned as the sound view, and that its meaning, that it goes to whoever holds authority after him, is that he spends it on what the Prophet ﷺ used to spend it on. The Prophet ﷺ said: "The one-fifth is returned to you," and this is clear, as you see.

It is not hidden that all the views concerning the share of the Prophet ﷺ after his death return to one thing: spending it on the interests of the Muslims.

The rightly guided caliphs, the rightly guided successors, may God be pleased with them, used to spend it on what the Prophet ﷺ used to spend it on.

Abu Bakr and 'Umar, may God be pleased with them both, used to spend it on horses and weapons.

The majority of scholars hold that the share of the near kin remains and did not lapse with his ﷺ death.

Scholars differed about it from three angles:

The first: does it lapse upon his death or not? We have mentioned that the sound view is that it does not lapse, contrary to Abu Hanifah.

The second: what is meant by the near kin?

The third: are their males given preference over their females or not?

As for the near kin, they are the Banu Hashim and the Banu al-Muttalib, according to the view best supported by evidence. This is the view of al-Shafi'i, Ahmad ibn Hanbal, Abu Thawr, Mujahid, Qatadah, Ibn Jurayj, and Muslim ibn Khalid.

al-Bukhari said in his Sahih, in the book "The Obligation of the Fifth": Abd Allah ibn Yusuf narrated to us, al-Layth narrated to us, from 'Uqayl, from Ibn Shihab, from Ibn al-Musayyab, from Jubayr ibn Mut'im, who said: "I and 'Uthman ibn 'Affan walked to the Messenger of God ﷺ and said: 'O Messenger of God, you gave to the Banu al-Muttalib and left us, though we and they are in one and the same position with respect to you.' The Messenger of God ﷺ said: 'The Banu al-Muttalib and the Banu Hashim are one and the same thing.'"

Al-Layth said: Yunus narrated to me, and added: Jubayr said: "The Prophet ﷺ did not give anything to the Banu 'Abd Shams or to the Banu Nawfal." End quote.

al-Bukhari also said in the Maghazi: Yahya ibn Bukayr narrated to us, al-Layth narrated to us, from Yunus, from Ibn Shihab, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, that Jubayr ibn Mut'im informed him, who said: "I and 'Uthman ibn 'Affan walked to the Prophet ﷺ and said: 'You gave the Banu al-Muttalib from the one-fifth of Khaybar and left us, though we are in one and the same position with respect to you.' He said: 'The Banu Hashim and the Banu al-Muttalib are one and the same thing.'" Jubayr said: "The Prophet ﷺ did not give anything to the Banu 'Abd Shams or the Banu Nawfal." End quote.

The explanation of why they are in one and the same position with respect to the Prophet ﷺ: Jubayr ibn Mut'im ibn 'Adi ibn Nawfal ibn 'Abd Manaf, and 'Uthman ibn 'Affan ibn Abi al-'As ibn 'Abd Shams ibn 'Abd Manaf.

The sons of 'Abd Manaf ibn Qusayy are four: Hashim, al-Muttalib, 'Abd Shams, and Nawfal.

They are full brothers through their mother 'Atikah, daughter of Murrah ibn Hilal al-Sulamiyyah, one of the 'Awatik of Sulaym, who are the grandmothers of the Messenger of God ﷺ, and they are three:

The one we have mentioned.

The second: her paternal aunt, who is 'Atikah daughter of Hilal, who was the mother of 'Abd Manaf.

The third: the daughter of the brother of the first, who is 'Atikah daughter of al-Awqas ibn Murrah ibn Hilal, and she is the mother of Wahb, the father of Aminah, the mother of the Prophet ﷺ.

The fourth son of 'Abd Manaf is Nawfal ibn 'Abd Manaf, whose mother was Waqidah daughter of Abi 'Adi, whose name is Nawfal ibn 'Ubadah ibn Mazin ibn Sa'sa'ah.

Shaykh Ahmad al-Badawi al-Shinqiti said in his verse "'Amud al-Nasab" [meter: rajaz]:
"'Abd Manaf, moon of al-Batha, four are his sons, these: al-Muttalib, Hashim, Nawfal, and 'Abd Shams; Hashim is not to be unknown."

And he said, explaining the 'Awatik of Sulaym who are his ﷺ grandmothers [rajaz]:
"The 'Awatik of the Prophet: Umm Wahb, Umm Hashim, and Umm al-Nadb, 'Abd Manaf's [mother], and this last one, the paternal aunt of the first, the little one."
"They in order are for the men: al-Awqas ibn Murrah ibn Hilal."

From what we have explained, it becomes clear that the sound view is that what is meant by the near kin in the verse is the Banu Hashim and the Banu al-Muttalib, not the Banu 'Abd Shams or the Banu Nawfal.

The reason is that the Banu 'Abd Shams and the Banu Nawfal opposed the Hashimites and backed Quraysh against them, so they became like distant relatives to them, because of enmity and lack of support.

For this reason Abu Talib said about them in his famous Lamiyyah [tawil meter]:
"May God repay us for 'Abd Shams and Nawfal, a punishment of evil, swift, not delayed.
With a scale of justice that does not cheat a grain, for which its own self is a witness, not a dependent.
The reason of a people has become foolish who changed, the sons of Khalaf, in place of us, and the Ghayatil.
And we are the pure core of the summit of Hashim and the family of Qusayy in the first calamities."

By this sound hadith we have cited, it becomes clear that the view of whoever says they are the Banu Hashim only is not correct, nor the view of whoever says they are all of Quraysh.

Among those who said they are the Banu Hashim only: 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz, Zayd ibn Arqam, Malik, al-Thawri, Mujahid, 'Ali ibn al-Husayn, al-Awza'i, and others.

al-Shafi'i, 'Abd al-Razzaq, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Muslim, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan transmitted from Ibn 'Abbas that Najdah al-Haruri wrote to him asking about the near kin whom God mentioned. He wrote back: "We used to hold that we are them, but our people refused this for us and said: Quraysh are all near kin."

The addition of his words "and they said: 'Quraysh are all'" was transmitted solely by Abu Ma'shar, and it has weakness.

What we have presented from the saying and the established action of the Prophet ﷺ in the Sahih specifies that they are the Banu Hashim and the Banu al-Muttalib, and this is the view of al-Shafi'i, Ahmad ibn Hanbal, and many people of knowledge.

Having understood that he ﷺ gave one-fifth of the one-fifth from the spoils of Khaybar to the Banu Hashim and the Banu al-Muttalib, and that they are the near kin mentioned in the verse:

Know that the scholars differed: are their males given preference over their females, or are they divided among them equally?

Some scholars held that it is like inheritance: the male receives the equivalent of the share of two females. This is the view of Ahmad ibn Hanbal in the more sound of the two narrations.

The author of al-Insaf said: This view was affirmed by al-Kharaqi, the author of al-Hidayah, al-Mudhhab, Masbuk al-Dhahab, al-'Umdah, al-Wajiz, and others; it was given precedence in al-Ri'ayatayn, al-Hawiyayn, and others, and was declared sound in al-Bulghah, al-Nazm, and others.

And there is a narration from him that male and female are equal. Ibn Rujayn gave it precedence in his commentary, and both views are stated without qualification in al-Mughni, al-Sharh, al-Muharrar, and al-Furu'. End quote from al-Insaf.

The preference of their males over their females, which is the view of Imam Ahmad, is also the view of al-Shafi'i.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 8, verse 41 (part 3 of 7):

The argument of those who said this view is that it is a share due by right of kinship to the father (qarabat al-ab) under the Sharia, as evidenced by the fact that the sons of his paternal aunts (ﷺ), such as al-Zubayr ibn al-'Awwam and 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Umayya, were not given a share in the one-fifth of the one-fifth; and that its being due solely by kinship to the father makes it like an inheritance, so the male is given preference over the female in it.

Some scholars said: its males and females are equal.

Among those who held this view were al-Muzani, Abu Thawr, and Ibn al-Mundhir.

The one who wrote this commentary, may Allah pardon him, says: This view is more evident to me, because preferring the male over the female requires evidence, and no evidence has been established for it in this matter, and no one has transmitted from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he preferred their males over their females in the one-fifth of the one-fifth.

The evidence that it is not like an inheritance is that a son among them takes his share while his father and grandfather are still alive. End of quote (ahhh).

Their small and their great are equal. The majority of scholars who hold that there is a share for the kinsmen hold that it is divided among all of them, and none of them is left out, unlike some groups.

The apparent meaning includes their wealthy as well as their poor, contrary to those who restricted it to their poor; because the Prophet (ﷺ) did not restrict it to their poor, unlike the share of orphans, the needy, and the wayfarer.

So the apparent meaning is that their poor alone are specified with it, and there is nothing for their wealthy. From what has preceded, it has become clear to you that the position of al-Shafi'i and Ahmad, may Allah have mercy on them both, in this matter, is that: the share of Allah and the share of His Messenger (ﷺ) is one; that after his death it is spent on the public interests of the Muslims; and that the share of the kinsmen belongs to the Banu Hashim and the Banu al-Muttalib, the male receiving the equivalent of the portion of two females; and that it belongs to all of them, rich and poor, whether they fought or did not fight; and that the males among them receive the equivalent of two females' portion; and that the remaining three shares are specifically for the poor among the orphans, the needy, and the wayfarer.

The position of Abu Hanifa: the share of the Messenger (ﷺ) and the share of his kinsmen lapse upon his death, and the one-fifth is divided among the remaining three: orphans, the needy, and the wayfarer.

He said: from the one-fifth one begins with the repair of bridges, the building of mosques, and the salaries of judges and soldiers. Something similar is also narrated from al-Shafi'i.

The position of Imam Malik, may Allah have mercy on him, is that the matter of the one-fifth of the spoils is left to the judgment and ijtihad (independent reasoning) of the Imam, in what he sees as beneficial; so he takes from it without fixed measure, gives to the kinsmen according to his ijtihad, and spends the remainder on the public interests of the Muslims.

Al-Qurtubi said in his tafsir of this noble verse under discussion: And with this view of Malik, the four caliphs spoke and acted, and it is indicated by his (ﷺ) saying: "My share of what Allah has returned to you is nothing but the one-fifth, and the one-fifth is returned to you," for he did not divide it into fifths or thirds; rather, he mentioned in the verse those he mentioned as a way of drawing attention to them, because they are among the most important to whom it is given.

Al-Zajjaj said, arguing for Malik: Allah, mighty and majestic, said: ﴿They ask you what they should spend. Say: Whatever good you spend is for parents and near relatives and orphans and the needy and the wayfarer﴾ [al-Baqarah: 215].

It is permissible for the ruler, by the consensus of scholars, to spend in other than these categories if he sees fit. An-Nasa'i narrated from 'Ata', who said: "The one-fifth of Allah and the one-fifth of His Messenger are one; the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would carry from it, give from it, and place it wherever he wished." End of quote from al-Qurtubi.

Ibn Kathir said in his tafsir of this noble verse, with the following text: "Others said: the one-fifth is disposed of by the Imam according to what is in the interest of the Muslims, just as property of fay' is disposed of."

Our shaykh, the scholar Ibn Taymiyya, said, may Allah have mercy on him: "This is the view of Malik and most of the early generation (salaf), and it is the most sound of the views." End of quote from Ibn Kathir.

This view is also the opinion of al-Bukhari, as shown by his statement: "Chapter: the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Then to Allah belongs one-fifth of it and to the Messenger﴾," meaning that the division of it belongs to the Messenger.

And the Messenger of Allah said: "I am only a divider and a treasurer, and Allah gives." Then al-Bukhari cited the hadiths of the chapter, concerning his (ﷺ) being a divider by the command of Allah, the Exalted.

The one who wrote this commentary, may Allah pardon him, says: This view is strong, and evidence for it will come, Allah willing, in the next issue; but the closest of the views to safety is acting on the apparent meaning of the verse, as al-Shafi'i and Ahmad, may Allah have mercy on them both, said; because Allah commanded us to know that the one-fifth of what we gained is for these mentioned purposes, and then followed that with His saying: ﴿if you have believed in Allah﴾, and this is very clear, as you see.

As for the statement of some of the People of the House, such as 'Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn 'Ali and 'Ali ibn al-Husayn, may Allah be pleased with them both, that the whole one-fifth belongs to them exclusively, and that what is meant by the orphans and the needy is their orphans and their needy; and the statement of one who claimed that after the Prophet (ﷺ) it goes to the kinsmen of the caliph whom the Muslims appoint, the weakness of both is not hidden. And Allah the Exalted knows best.

* *

The third issue: The scholars agreed that gold, silver, and all other goods are all included in the ruling of the verse: one-fifth is taken out, and the remainder is divided among the spoilers, as we mentioned.

The fourth issue: As for their land taken by force ('anwatan), the scholars differed concerning it. Some scholars said: the Imam is given the choice between dividing it, as is done with gold and silver, with no kharaj upon it, rather it is land of 'ushr owned by the spoilers; and between keeping it as a waqf for the Muslims by a formula. And it was said: without a formula; and this includes leaving it to the Muslims in exchange for a continuous kharaj taken from whoever remains on it. This option is the position of Imam Ahmad.

On this view: if the Imam divides it, it was said: it is subject to the one-fifth, and this is the more evident; and it was said: no. Some eminent scholars chose this, saying: the land of Khaybar, the part of it that was divided was not subjected to the one-fifth.

The apparent view is that the land of Khaybar was subjected to the one-fifth, as many have affirmed, and Abu Dawud narrated it with a sound chain from al-Zuhri.

This choice between division and keeping it for the Muslims, which we mentioned is the position of Imam Ahmad, is also the position of Imam Abu Hanifa and al-Thawri.

As for Malik, may Allah have mercy on him, he held that it becomes a waqf for the Muslims merely by seizing it.

As for al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him, he held that it is spoils which must be divided among the fighters, after the one-fifth is taken out; and we will mention, Allah willing, the proofs of all, and what appears to us to be preponderant by evidence.

As for the proof of Imam al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him, it is from the Book and the Sunna.

As for the Book: the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And know that whatever you gain of any thing﴾, the verse, which by its generality requires the inclusion of the captured land.

As for the Sunna: it is established that he (ﷺ) divided the land of Qurayza after taking out the one-fifth from it, and that of the Banu al-Nadir, and he halved the land of Khaybar among the spoilers.

He said: If it were permissible to claim the exclusion of the land, it would be permissible to claim the exclusion of other things, and the ruling of the verse would be nullified.

The one who wrote this commentary, may Allah pardon him, says: The derivation from the verse is evident; from the Sunna it is not evident, because there is no proof in it against the one who says there is a choice: for he says: he had the choice and chose division, so division is not obligatory; and this is clear, as you see.

The argument of those who said there is a choice: the Prophet (ﷺ) divided half of the land of Khaybar and left the other half, divided the land of Qurayza and left the division of Makkah; so his dividing at one time and his leaving division at another indicates the choice.

In the "Sunan" and the "Mustadrak": "When the Prophet (ﷺ) gained control of Khaybar, he divided it into thirty-six shares, each share collected from a hundred shares; so the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and the Muslims had half of that, and he set aside the other half for those who came to him of the delegations, the affairs, and the calamities of the people." This is the wording of Abu Dawud.

In another wording: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) set aside eighteen shares, which is the half, for his calamities and what befell him of the affairs of the Muslims; and that was al-Watih, al-Kutayba, al-Salalim, and their dependencies."

Also in another wording: "He set aside half of it for his calamities and what befell him: al-Watiha, al-Kutayba, and what was granted with them; and he set aside the other half and divided it among the Muslims: al-Shaqq, al-Nata, and what was granted with them; and the Messenger of Allah's (ﷺ) share was in what was granted with them."

The opponent rejected this argument, saying that the divided half of Khaybar was taken by force, and the undivided half of it was taken by treaty; and Ibn Hajar affirmed this in "Fath al-Bari."

And al-Nawawi said in "Sharh Muslim," in discussing the statement of Anas in Muslim: "and we took it by force," the following text: al-Qadi said: al-Mazari said: The apparent meaning of this is that all of it was conquered by force; but Malik narrated from Ibn Shihab that part of it was conquered by force and part by treaty. He said: What is narrated in Abu Dawud's Sunan may be problematic, that he divided it into two halves: a half for his calamities and need, and a half for the Muslims. He said: Its answer is what some of them said: that around it were estates and villages whose people had been expelled, so they were exclusively for the Prophet (ﷺ), and what was other than them for the spoilers; the extent of what they had left was half, and for this it was divided into two halves. End of quote in his wording.

Abu Dawud said in his Sunan: Husayn ibn 'Ali al-'Ijli narrated to us, Yahya, that is Ibn Adam, narrated to us, Ibn Abi Za'ida narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from al-Zuhri, and 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Bakr, and some of the sons of Muhammad ibn Maslama, who said: "A remnant of the people of Khaybar remained, who fortified themselves, and they asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to preserve their blood and let them go, and he did so. The people of Fadak heard of that, and they came down on the same terms, so it was exclusively for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), because it had not been obtained with horses or riding camels."

Muhammad ibn Yahya ibn Faris narrated to us, 'Abd Allah ibn Muhammad narrated to us, from Juwayriya, from Malik, from al-Zuhri: that Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab informed him: "That the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) conquered part of Khaybar by force."

Abu Dawud said: It was read to al-Harith ibn Miskin while I was present, Ibn Wahb informed them, saying: Malik narrated to me, from Ibn Shihab: that Khaybar was partly by force and partly by treaty, and al-Kutayba was mostly by force with some treaty in it. I said to Malik: What is al-Kutayba? He said: The land of Khaybar, and it is forty thousand palm-trunks.

The one who wrote this commentary, may Allah pardon him, says: What we have mentioned undermines the argument for the Imam's choice regarding division; and the exclusivity of the Khaybar case is as you see. The argument of Malik, may Allah have mercy on him, and whoever agreed with him, that the land of the enemy conquered by force becomes a waqf for the Muslims merely by seizing it, consists of several matters:

Among them: the Prophet's (ﷺ) saying established in Sahih Muslim from the hadith of Abu Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with him: "The Iraq has been denied its dirham and its qafiz, Syria has been denied its modius and its dinar, Egypt has been denied its ardabb and its dinar, and you will return from where you began, you will return from where you began, you will return from where you began; Abu Hurayra's flesh and blood bears witness to that."

The way they argue from the hadith is that: "has been denied" means "will be denied," and he used the past tense to announce the certainty of its occurrence, like His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And the Trumpet will be blown﴾, the verse [al-Kahf: 99], and [Ya-Sin: 51], [al-Zumar: 68], and [al-Nahl: 1], and His saying: ﴿The command of Allah has come﴾, the verse.

They said: This indicates that it does not belong to the spoilers, because what the spoilers own does not have a qafiz or a dirham in it. And for the hadith of Muslim there is a witness from the hadith of Jabir in Muslim as well, and from the hadith of Abu Hurayra also in al-Bukhari.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 8, verse 41 (part 4 of 7):

Ibn Hajar said in *Fath al-Bari* (*The Opening of the Creator*, his commentary on Sahih al-Bukhari), in the book "The Obligation of the Fifth" (*fard al-khums*, the one-fifth share of the spoils), the following: Ibn Hazm mentioned that some of the Malikis argued, with the Prophet's (ﷺ) saying in the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, "Iraq has been denied its dirham," and the rest of the hadith, that conquered land (*al-ard al-maghnumah*) may not be sold or divided, and that the meaning of "denial" is the denial of the kharaj (land tax). He answered this by saying that the hadith was given as a warning about the evil consequence that would come, namely that the Muslims would eventually be denied their rights, and that this indeed happened.

They also argued with what is established in the Sahih from Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: "Were it not for the last of the Muslims, no town would have been conquered except that I would have divided it among its people, just as the Prophet (ﷺ) divided Khaybar."

In another wording in the Sahih from Umar: "By He in whose hand is my soul, were it not that I would leave the last of the people as orphaned beggars with nothing, no town would have been conquered by me except that I would have divided it, just as the Prophet (ﷺ) divided Khaybar. But I leave it as a treasury for them to share."

Those who held this view also argued: if conquered land were divided, nothing would remain for those who came after the fighters (*al-ghanimin*). Allah has established a share for those who came after them with His saying: ﴿And those who came after them say: "Our Lord, forgive us..."﴾ [al-Hashr: 10], for it is conjoined to His saying: ﴿for the poor emigrants who were expelled﴾ [al-Hashr: 8], and His saying: ﴿and those who had settled the abode and the faith﴾ [al-Hashr: 9]. As for the view of the one who said that His saying, exalted is He, ﴿And those who came after them﴾ is a subject (*mubtada'*) whose predicate is "they say," it is not correct, because it would imply that He, exalted is He, informed that everyone who comes after them says: ﴿Our Lord, forgive us and our brothers...﴾ and so on.

The reality is otherwise, because many of those who came after them revile and curse the Companions. The truth is that His saying ﴿And those who came﴾ is conjoined to what precedes it, and the clause "they say" is a circumstantial clause (*hal*), as was explained earlier in Surat Al 'Imran. It is a qualifier of its own verb and a descriptor of its subject.

(p-70) The one who qualifies it, may Allah pardon him, said: These proofs which the Malikis cited do not stand, as far as it appears. This is because the mentioned hadiths do not clearly establish the point of evidence in them, since it is possible that the Imam had the choice, and he chose to leave them for the Muslims, and it was not obligatory at the outset, as we have previously stated.

The use of the aforementioned verse of al-Hashr is clearly invalid, because it concerns *fay'* (booty obtained without battle), whereas the discussion is about *ghanimah* (war spoils), and the difference between them is known, as we have previously stated.

The one who qualifies it, may Allah pardon him, said: The view with the strongest evidence is that the Imam has the choice. The statement of Umar in the report just passed supports this, and with it the proofs come together, and there is no contradiction among them. Reconciliation is obligatory whenever it is possible.

The most that can be said in this matter is that the Sunnah indicates a specification (*takhsis*) of the general wording of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And know that whatever you acquire as spoils...﴾ [al-Anfal: 41].

The specification of the Book by the Sunnah is common.

Al-Qurtubi said in his commentary on this verse which we are now dealing with, after mentioning the view of optionality (*al-takhyir*), the following: "Our shaykh Abu al-Abbas (may Allah be pleased with him) said: It seems this is a reconciliation between the two evidences and a middle course between the two positions, and it is what Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) understood with certainty. That is why he said: 'Were it not for the last of the people,' and he did not report the abrogation (*naskh*) of the Prophet's (ﷺ) action, nor its restriction to those people."

If it is said: There is no contradiction among the evidences according to the school of al-Shafi'i, because what was divided at Khaybar was taken by force (*'anwatan*), and what was not divided of it was taken by treaty (*sulhan*), and al-Nadir was fay', and Qurayzah was divided.

If someone were to say: it is also fay', because they surrendered to the judgment of the Prophet (ﷺ) before he appointed Sa'd to judge over them, that would not be far-fetched. But what refutes it is that the Prophet (ﷺ) took one-fifth of it, as Malik and others stated.

Makkah was taken by treaty, as evidenced by his (ﷺ) saying: "Whoever enters the house of Abu Sufyan is safe, whoever lays down his weapons is safe, and whoever closes his door is safe." This is established in Sahih Muslim.

The answer is that the verified position is that Makkah was taken by force, and there is clear evidence for this.

Among these is that no one has reported that the Prophet (ﷺ) made a treaty with its people at the time of the conquest, nor did any of them come to him and make a treaty with him concerning the city. Rather, Abu Sufyan came to him and he granted him safe-conduct for whoever enters his house, closes his door, enters the mosque, or lays down his weapons.

Had it been taken by treaty, he would not have said: "Whoever enters his house, or closes his door, or enters the mosque, is safe," for a treaty implies a general safe-conduct.

Among them also: the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Allah withheld the elephant from Makkah and gave power over it to His Messenger and the believers, and He permitted me to enter it for an hour of the day."

In another wording: "It was not lawful for anyone before me, and it will not be lawful for anyone after me, but it was made lawful for me for an hour of the day."

In another wording: "If anyone uses the permission for fighting the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) as an excuse, say: Allah permitted His Messenger, but He did not permit you. He permitted me only for an hour of the day, and its sanctity has returned today as it was yesterday." This is explicit that it was taken by force.
